description: The researchers introduced three word embedding methods and three classifiers as a toolkit for predicting item quality for accessible assessments.
title: Machine-learning prediction of accessible assessment-item quality

description: The Making-Process-Rug is a visual video-analysis method developed by the authors to trace \"social-discursive, materially mediated, individual, and collaborative making processes\" across a longitudinal co-invention project.
title: Making-Process-Rug video-analysis method

description: MFRM, developed by Linacre in 1989 as an extension of the partial credit model, is an IRT model in which \"all so urces of variability , such as raters, items and persons, which have the potential to influence measurement results , are considered simultaneously\".
title: Many-Facet Rasch Model

description: The existing tool, built in T-SQL within the Growth Research Database, runs an automated pipeline: data cleaning, item parameter estimation via a brute-force grid search over RIT values 100-350 that minimizes mean square fit with person abilities fixed, and a Model of Man (MoM) procedure that predic
title: MAP Growth item calibration workflow

description: The article adapts a counterfactual framework for time-varying treatments in which \"Inverse probability of treatment (IPT) weighting is an alternative approach specifically developed to adjust for confounding by time-varying covariates.\" A marginal structural model specifies the logit of graduation
title: Marginal structural models with inverse probability of treatment weighting

description: The article recommends that researchers gauge the stability of longitudinal growth estimates by comparing techniques assuming MAR against those assuming MNAR.
title: MAR–MNAR missing-data sensitivity analysis for longitudinal educational research

description: The article formalizes the integration of reading activity data and reading content data as a matrix multiplication between traditional reading logs and a matrix M encoding topic distributions across pages of the reading material.
title: Matrix-based multimodal integration of reading activity and content data

description: The article proposes representing peer assessment as a sparse three-dimensional matrix (graders × answers × labels) and completing it via matrix factorization.
title: Matrix factorization model of peer assessment with ordinal preference learning

description: Large-scale assessments organize items into testlets counterbalanced across students within a sampling frame, so that 'no student ever takes the entire battery of assessments, or even all the items on any one test'.
title: Matrix sampling with planned missingness in large-scale assessments
